name: Shipping container (40 ft)
headline: length
subtitle: Standard 40 ft general-purpose container (8 ft 6 in high)
description: Standard steel shipping containers are built to external sizes set by the international standard ISO 668, so they stack and lock together on ships, trains and trucks. A 40 ft general-purpose container measures 12,192 mm long, 2,438 mm wide and 2,591 mm (8 ft 6 in) high on the outside. Shipping line Hapag-Lloyd lists its 40 ft boxes at about 3.7 tonnes empty with 67.7 cubic metres of cargo space.

measures.label: External height
measures.note: 8 ft 6 in standard container; high-cube containers are 9 ft 6 in (2,896 mm)

facts.text: ISO 668 sets a minimum internal size for a 40 ft container of 12,029 mm long, 2,350 mm wide and 2,350 mm high.
A standard 20 ft container is 6,058 mm long, a little under half the length of a 40 ft container.
Some of Hapag-Lloyd's 40 ft general-purpose container series can carry up to 28,800 kg of cargo.

sources.title: Container Specification (external and minimum internal dimensions according to ISO 668; 40' general purpose container)

caveats: The ISO 668 standard itself is sold, not published free; the dimensions are taken from Hapag-Lloyd's specification, which reproduces the ISO 668 table.
Weights and capacity are for Hapag-Lloyd's fleet and vary slightly by manufacturer.
